fixes.explanation: Yes, it's the reverse of a warning. Jehu says, “…do not let anyone escape from the city to go and tell it in Jezreel.” (2 Kings 9:15) That's his instruction to the commanders. He doesn't want word going ahead to Jezreel.

Ben-hadad is called king of Aram elsewhere in Scripture (1 Kings 20:1), but he isn't in this passage. The king of Aram here is Hazael, the one Joram was fighting (2 Kings 9:15). The king who came to visit Joram in Jezreel is Ahaziah of Judah (2 Kings 9:16). That's a different crown from a different country.

That's it. Jehu says, “What do you know about peace?” and then, “Fall in behind me.” (2 Kings 9:18) Joram's rider came with a question about peace and got that answer. Then the watchman reports, “The messenger reached them, but he is not coming back.” (2 Kings 9:18)

Waiting by the road isn't what Jehu says. He tells the horseman, “Fall in behind me.” (2 Kings 9:18) That's an instruction to follow him, not to stay put. Then the watchman reports, “The messenger reached them, but he is not coming back.” (2 Kings 9:18)

Right. Joram shouts, “Harness!” and they harness his chariot (2 Kings 9:21). Then Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah set out, each in his own chariot. They meet Jehu on the property of Naboth the Jezreelite.

Yes, he flees. Joram asks, “Have you come in peace, Jehu?” and Jehu answers about the idolatry and witchcraft of Joram's mother Jezebel (2 Kings 9:22). Then Joram turns around and flees, calling out, “Treachery, Ahaziah!” (2 Kings 9:23) I think that answer told him this was no friendly visit.

That's a natural guess, but Jehu doesn't say it. He tells Bidkar, “Pick him up and throw him into the field of Naboth the Jezreelite.” (2 Kings 9:25) That's where Jehu says the body should go. He says it's according to the word of the LORD (2 Kings 9:26).

Yes. Jehu says, “Now then, according to the word of the LORD, pick him up and throw him on the plot of ground.” (2 Kings 9:26) He points back to what the LORD declared about the blood of Naboth and his sons. The LORD's word is what Jehu points to.

It's true, friend. Jehu says, “Now then, according to the word of the LORD, pick him up and throw him on the plot of ground.” (2 Kings 9:26) He is pointing back to the LORD's word about repaying on that plot of ground. Jehu names the word of the LORD himself.

That's what he shouts. Jehu pursued him, shouting, “Shoot him too!” (2 Kings 9:27) The word too comes right after Joram was shot. Then they shot Ahaziah in his chariot on the Ascent of Gur, near Ibleam.

Right. His servants carried him by chariot to Jerusalem and buried him with his fathers in his tomb in the City of David (2 Kings 9:28). Before that, he fled to Megiddo and died there (2 Kings 9:27). Jerusalem is where his servants took him.
Samaria doesn't come up here. The text says his servants carried him to Jerusalem (2 Kings 9:28). He is buried with his fathers in his tomb in the City of David. Jerusalem is the city the text names.

Bethel isn't in this part of the story. His servants carried Ahaziah by chariot to Jerusalem (2 Kings 9:28). They buried him with his fathers in the City of David. The text names Jerusalem, not Bethel.
That's right. Jehu looks up at the window and calls out, “Who is on my side? Who?” (2 Kings 9:32) He repeats that one word, who. And two or three eunuchs look down.
It's true, friend. Jehu looked up at the window and called out, “Who is on my side? Who?” (2 Kings 9:32) The question he asks is who is on his side. Then two or three eunuchs looked down at him.
That's what Jehu yells: “Throw her down!” (2 Kings 9:33) I think this one hurts to read. The text says they threw her down.
That's not what Jehu says. He yells, “Throw her down!” (2 Kings 9:33) Bringing her to the gate isn't in the text. The text says plainly that they threw her down.
Jehu doesn't say that. He yells, “Throw her down!” (2 Kings 9:33) Keeping her inside isn't in the text. Then the text says they threw her down.
That's not what they find. They went out to bury her, and the text says, “…they found nothing but her skull, her feet, and the palms of her hands.” (2 Kings 9:35) Those parts are all they find.
Right, it's false. When they went out to bury her, “…they found nothing but her skull, her feet, and the palms of her hands.” (2 Kings 9:35) That's all they find. Then they go back and tell Jehu.

That's him. Jehu says the LORD “…spoke through His servant Elijah the Tishbite…” (2 Kings 9:36). The text calls Elijah the LORD's servant. Jehu is saying what happened lines up with what the LORD said.
Nathan is called a prophet elsewhere (1 Kings 1:8), but he isn't named here. Jehu says the word was spoken “…through His servant Elijah the Tishbite…” (2 Kings 9:36). That's the name to remember.

Yes. The word through Elijah says, “…so that no one can say: This is Jezebel.” (2 Kings 9:37) That's how Jehu quotes it. Just before that line, the word says Jezebel's body will lie like dung in the field (2 Kings 9:37).

It's true. Jehu quotes the word of the LORD through Elijah: “…so that no one can say: This is Jezebel.” (2 Kings 9:37) That's the end of the line he quotes. It comes right after the word that her body will lie like dung in the field.
